# onpager_outgoing_webhook (Resource)

Manage one tenant outgoing webhook definition, HTTP request configuration and named credentials.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Passive configuration example: no HTTP delivery is performed by Terraform.
resource "onpager_outgoing_webhook" "example" {
  purpose      = "escalation"
  display_name = "Terraform passive webhook"
  enabled      = false

  request = {
    method          = "POST"
    endpoint        = "https://automation.example.invalid/onpager"
    body_format     = "json"
    body_template   = "{{ json .Notification }}"
    verify_ssl      = true
    timeout_seconds = 5
    headers = [{
      key   = "X-OnPager-Source"
      value = "terraform"
    }]
    auth = { kind = "none" }
  }
}

# Credential example: declare secrets = { token = { action = "replace",
# value = var.webhook_token } } and request.auth = { kind = "bearer",
# token_secret = "token" }. Mark webhook_token sensitive; it persists in state.
```

## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Nonblank UTF-8 display name, at most 200 characters, without leading or trailing whitespace. Updated in place; no default.
- `purpose` (String) Immutable `notification` or `escalation` purpose. Notification definitions may declare recipient fields; escalation definitions must omit them. Changing purpose replaces this resource.
- `request` (Attributes) Typed HTTP request definition. The API validates templates when saving. The provider never renders, previews, tests or delivers it. Use named secrets for credentials; all configured fields persist in Terraform state. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--request))

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the webhook is enabled. Defaults to `true`. Disabled definitions remain readable and can be enabled again. Saving a definition performs no HTTP delivery.
- `recipient_fields` (Attributes List) Ordered notification-recipient field declarations, at most 20. Omitted/null or empty means no fields. Forbidden for escalation purpose. Existing enabled personal methods may prevent incompatible changes; the provider never edits them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--recipient_fields))
- `request_id` (String) Create idempotency UUID. When omitted, it remains unknown while planning and a fresh UUID is generated during each create/replacement, then saved in state. An explicit nonzero canonical lowercase UUID supports recovery/replay with the same principal, scope and exact initial payload. Changing an explicit key requires replacement; use a fresh explicit key for intentional replacements. Import cannot recover it and leaves it null. The provider never retries mutations automatically.
- `secrets` (Attributes Map) Explicit named credential changes (at most 50 keys and 65,536 total value bytes). Omitted/null or empty maps preserve stored credentials; omitted individual keys also preserve them. Only action `delete` removes a credential. Known configured values survive refresh while the API confirms the key exists. Import cannot recover values. Configured values persist in Terraform state. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secrets))

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) This definition's strong numeric ETag, validated against the response body and used for PUT/DELETE `If-Match`. Concurrent changes fail; no collection or parent revision is substituted.
- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `runtime_status` (String) Backend runtime availability (`ready`, `disabled`, or `unavailable`). Availability is observed without invoking or testing the webhook.
- `secret_keys` (List of String) Names of credentials the API confirms are present. GET never returns their values; import can recover names only.

<a id="nestedatt--request"></a>
### Nested Schema for `request`

Required:

- `endpoint` (String) Absolute HTTP(S) endpoint template, at most 8192 bytes. Host and scheme must be literal; user information and fragments are forbidden. Query parameters may be declared here or in `query`; the API stores them as ordered pairs. No request is sent to this endpoint during Terraform operations.

Optional:

- `auth` (Attributes) Authentication references; defaults to `none`. These fields name secrets rather than returning or exposing credential values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--request--auth))
- `body_format` (String) Body format: `json` (default), `form`, or `text`. Form bodies use only `form`; JSON/text bodies use `body_template`.
- `body_template` (String) Exact body template, at most 65,536 bytes. Defaults to the empty string. Omitted/null selects the default; explicit empty clears the template. Form and GET/HEAD requests require empty content.
- `content_type` (String) Optional media type for `text` bodies only. Defaults to empty, selecting the API's default. JSON/form media types are controlled by `body_format`.
- `form` (Attributes List) URL-encoded form pairs, supported only for `body_format = "form"`. Ordered list of at most 50 pairs; duplicate query/form keys are allowed. Omitted/null and empty lists both configure no pairs. Templates are limited to 65,536 bytes per value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--request--form))
- `headers` (Attributes List) Header pairs. Names must be unique case-insensitively; transport/reserved headers are forbidden. Explicit Authorization conflicts with basic/bearer auth. Ordered list of at most 50 pairs; duplicate query/form keys are allowed. Omitted/null and empty lists both configure no pairs. Templates are limited to 65,536 bytes per value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--request--headers))
- `method` (String) Uppercase HTTP method: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE`. Defaults to `POST`. GET/HEAD require an empty body and no form pairs.
- `query` (Attributes List) Query string pairs appended after endpoint parameters are parsed. Ordered list of at most 50 pairs; duplicate query/form keys are allowed. Omitted/null and empty lists both configure no pairs. Templates are limited to 65,536 bytes per value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--request--query))
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Destination request timeout in whole seconds, from 1 through 60 inclusive. Defaults to `5`; zero is invalid.
- `verify_ssl` (Boolean) Verify destination TLS certificates. Defaults to `true`; explicit false disables destination verification only, without changing provider Control TLS verification.

### Nested Schema for `request.auth`

Optional:

- `kind` (String) Authentication kind: `none` (default), `basic`, or `bearer`.
- `password_secret` (String) Named password secret for basic authentication. Empty means no password. Forbidden for none/bearer; defaults to empty.
- `token_secret` (String) Named credential required for bearer authentication; forbidden for none/basic. Defaults to empty.
- `username` (String) Basic-auth username. Required for basic, forbidden for none/bearer. Must not contain a colon or control characters. Defaults to empty.

### Nested Schema for `secrets`

Required:

- `action` (String) `replace` writes `value` (including explicit empty); `keep` requires an existing key and sends no value; `delete` removes this key. No action is inferred from omission.

Optional:

## Import

Import using `webhook_uuid`. Import reads the exact tenant-scoped URL, including
disabled definitions. Missing, foreign-tenant and wrong-route UUIDs return HTTP
404; denied existing definitions return HTTP 403 and retain state.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_outgoing_webhook.example
  id = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_outgoing_webhook.example 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222
```

## Lifecycle

This resource owns one tenant outgoing webhook definition. Purpose is immutable;
changing it requires replacement. Other request and settings changes use PUT
with the definition's saved strong numeric ETag. Refresh and import use direct
reads.

Destroy sends DELETE with the saved ETag and disables the definition. Its UUID,
history and credentials remain; disabled definitions are directly readable. Only
confirmed absence removes state. Authorization, transport and other API errors
retain it. Concurrent writes require a new plan; the provider does not
substitute a newer revision.

## Create identity and recovery

Optional `request_id` is the create idempotency key. When omitted, it remains
unknown during planning; each create or replacement generates a fresh UUID
during apply and saves it in state. Updates preserve that key. Dependency
expressions remain unresolved until their values are known. A saved plan does
not preselect an automatically generated key.

Configure an explicit UUID for deterministic replay or recovery. Repeating the
exact initial payload with the same principal, scope and key can recover a
create; changing that payload under the same key conflicts. Use a fresh explicit
key for intentional replacement. Import cannot recover the key and leaves it
null. Mutations are not retried automatically.

A known UUID and confirmed committed settings remain in state if a success
receipt is incomplete. If a create receipt has no usable UUID, investigate
whether creation committed before applying again. An automatically generated key
may be unavailable for recovery.

## Credentials and state

The `secrets` map declares explicit credential changes. `replace` requires a
non-null value; an empty string writes an empty credential. `keep` requires an
existing key; `delete` removes that credential. For keep and delete, omit
`value` or use null or empty. Omitting the map, using null or an empty map, or
omitting an individual key preserves saved credentials. Removing a map entry
does not delete a credential. Keys match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}`; at most
50 changes and 65,536 total value bytes are supported.

The API returns credential names and presence flags, not values. Configured
values survive refresh while their keys remain present. Import recovers
`secret_keys` only. After import, omit `secrets` to retain saved credentials or
configure explicit replacements. Sensitive values still persist in Terraform
state and saved plans. Request templates and other configured fields also
persist in state; reference `.Secrets.key` rather than embedding credentials.

Query and form pair order and duplicate keys are preserved. The API normalizes
inline endpoint query parameters into pairs. Optional pair and recipient lists
use no entries when omitted, null or explicitly empty. Personal recipient values
and dependent configuration are managed separately; resolve dependency conflicts
explicitly.

## Permissions

Requires tenant-scoped grants `outgoing_webhooks.read`,
`outgoing_webhooks.create`, `outgoing_webhooks.update` and
`outgoing_webhooks.disable`, including for service accounts. Credential changes
and request changes that use saved credentials additionally require
`outgoing_webhooks.credentials.update`. Preview and use grants are not required.
The server must have runtime credential-key configuration; HTTP 503
`webhook_credentials_unavailable` requires deployment configuration to be fixed.
